purpose: The named vessels of the limbs drawn on both bodies (owner, 18 November 2026: "let's get the vascularity right ... and for all other items as well").
derivation: For each BodyParts3D 4.0 vessel mesh (byte-exact archive member, sha256 below): from every vertex a ray along its normal to the opposite wall gives an axis point (the midpoint) and a radius (half the wall-to-wall distance); axis points are averaged in 2 mm cells, cells within 6 mm linked, the longest paths of each group's spanning tree kept as the vessel's trunk and branches (at least 18 mm; pieces under 12 mm dropped), smoothed and resampled every 3 mm. The coarse femoral meshes (edges of about 1 cm) are cut in 8 mm slices along their main axis instead (method "slices"). Points are [x, y, z, radius] in the BodyParts3D 4.0 whole-body frame, millimetres. The game rebuilds round tubes from them and rivets them to the drawn muscles and bones; the meshes themselves are not shipped.

source.atlas: BodyParts3D 4.0, The Database Center for Life Science (DBCLS)

not_included: neck: the atlas's common carotid (FJ3483, FJ3564) and internal jugular (FJ3485, FJ3585) pieces are 6 to 65 mm stubs; the external jugular vein is not in BodyParts3D 4.0
the intercostal vessels: hidden under the ribs and the chest muscles
the left arm's vessels on your own body: your left arm is the game arm, drawn and skinned by its own rig; not wired here
